title_en: Psychology Made Simple (18/20): Splitting the Page in Two
note_en: The 把 construction moves the object before the verb when something is done to it with a result: 把它分成两半 "divide it into two halves," 把想法写在纸上 "write your thoughts down on paper." After 把 + object, the verb must be followed by a result or destination (分成两半, 写在纸上); a bare 把它分 is incomplete. English simply says "split the page," but Chinese uses 把 to stress what happens to the object.
